correctness.rationale: For an extraspecial \(p\)-group, the commutator descends to a nondegenerate alternating form on \(G/Z(G)\). Projective fibers have size \(s=p(p-1)\) and are exactly the maximal false-twin classes. Two omissions in one class force identical distance vectors and a fixed-point stabilizing transposition. With at most one omission per class, adjacent quotient points are separated by a retained vertex in one class, while orthogonal quotient points are separated by a retained vertex over the symmetric difference of their distinct polar hyperplanes. The same retained vertices force every maximal twin class setwise and hence every vertex pointwise. This proves the if-and-only-if characterization for both invariants and the factorized polynomial. Direct projective and Heisenberg computations replay successfully.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural classification across the entire extraspecial family: it identifies every resolving set and every determining set, proves the two families coincide, and derives the exact common minimum and full subset enumerator. The mechanism is structural—projective fibers of the nondegenerate commutator form—not a table recomputation. It supplies a sharp benchmark for extending symmetry and metric questions from extraspecial groups to more general class-two groups.
